history.summary: A major Shakti shrine atop a hillock about 3 km from the Vindhyavasini temple at Vindhyachal. Goddess Ashtabhuja (eight-armed) is identified here with Mahasaraswati/Yogmaya: tradition says she slipped from Kansa's grasp after Krishna's birth and settled on the Vindhya hills (Durga Saptashati of the Markandeya Purana calls the goddess 'Vindhyachal Nivasini'). The temple is the third point of the Trikon Parikrama, after Vindhyavasini and Kali Khoh; ~160 steps lead up, and a cave shrine is associated with Markandeya Rishi. name: Ashtabhuja Temple
town_description: Vindhyachal is a pilgrimage town in Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Ganga, forming with Mirzapur a single urban agglomeration. It is one of the principal Shakti Peethas of India, centred on the Vindhyavasini temple, with the Ashtabhuja and Kali Khoh temples completing the Trikon Parikrama triangle.
